change_of_basis: v1 named detect-secrets and pip-licenses, both third-party, but the SBOM was hand-written and no third-party vulnerability source was consulted. v2 replaces the SBOM with a CycloneDX 1.6 document generated by cyclonedx-bom and adds pip-audit against the PyPI advisory database. Every figure below comes from a tool this round did not write.
scope_statement: The three SP ZIPs are SOURCE distributions; they do not bundle wheels. The audit therefore measures the runtime environment that satisfies their declared dependencies, which is the closest available measurement and NOT a claim that the ZIPs ship vulnerable code.
conclusion: The three scans TS11 asks for are now third-party and reproducible. They are not clean: disk shows 68 advisories across 9 packages in the host runtime, 9 of which have a published fix. Distributability is therefore conditional: see FAR_R14_5 for the deviation.
claim_ceiling: THREE_MIT_SOURCE_ZIPS_DISTRIBUTABLE_NO_DECLARED_DEPENDENCIES; host runtime advisories out of scope and registered

deliverable_dependency_closure.method: tomllib over the three packages' pyproject.toml in build_a and build_b
deliverable_dependency_closure.finding: All three SP packages declare ZERO runtime dependencies and are MIT. The 68 advisories therefore sit entirely in the host Hermes runtime, outside the deliverables' dependency closure; none of them is a statement about code shipped in the ZIPs.

licences.note: the single UNKNOWN licence distribution in the environment is agent-client-protocol 0.9.0, which none of the three packages depends on
